chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from al-A'ala ibn Razin, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:
Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) was asked about the man who leads the people in prayer and makes a mistake. He (peace be upon him) said: 'The one behind him corrects him.'

key_terms.يَفْتَحُ عَلَيْهِ: he corrects him / opens for him

ai.seo_question: What should followers do if the Imam makes a mistake during prayer?
ai.summary: In this narration from al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the mechanism of *takhjij* (correction) during congregational prayer, specifying that the follower directly behind the imam must verbally correct the imam's recitation error. This ruling underscores the hierarchical yet interactive nature of Shia jurisprudence, where the validity of the imam's prayer is maintained through the active participation of the *ma'mum*, reflecting the principle that the follower's role is not merely passive but essential for the ritual's integrity. The emphasis on the person 'behind' highlights the specific chain of command in the prayer row, ensuring that errors are rectified immediately without disrupting the flow of worship.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Al Hakam, from Al A’ala Bin Razeyn, from Muhammad Bin Muslim who said,
‘Abu Abdullahasws was asked about the man leading the people in Salāt, so he commits a mistake’. Heasws said: ‘He would correct him, the one behind him’.
en.sarwar: 23. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn al-Hakam from al-’Ala’ ibn Razin from Muhammad ibn Muslim who has said the following:
“Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, was asked about a man who leads people in Salah (prayer) and makes a mistake. He (the Imam) said, ‘Those behind him open it up for him (help to correct him).”’
